The lane's only other in-flight work (#7529 / PR #8902) is in `packages/lint` + `packages/metadata-protocol`, disjoint.

## Model tier — upgraded from triage's suggestion, with reason

Triage suggested `sonnet` (`5302838248`, "S mechanical"). **Dispatching at `opus`.** The version-number substitution is mechanical, but the card also asks for prose rewritten *as shipped*, a judgement about whether other pre-mode framing survived the 16.0.0 cut, and whether a `Landed since 16.0.0-rc.N` window was left open. That is editorial judgement on a **release-owned** page, and there is no gate that will catch getting it wrong — the failure mode is a plausible-sounding wrong sentence, which is exactly what the `sonnet` floor is not for. The suggestion is an input, not a decision; ⛔ not taken here, and this is the reason.

## Premise re-check — performed at 2026-08-15T16:12Z on `origin/main` @ `85f5e78`, all four confirmed

| card's claim | measured |
|:--|:--|
| `v16.mdx` blockquote still says "currently published as `16.0.0-rc.0`" | ✅ present, at the stated location |
| `index.mdx` v16 entry ends `(current series: 16.0.0-rc.0)` | ✅ **line 22**, verbatim |
| v16 actually went GA and took a minor | ✅ `git tag --list '@objectstack/spec@16*'` ⇒ `16.0.0`, `16.0.0-rc.0`, `16.0.0-rc.1`, **`16.1.0`** |
| v16 is the *second* entry claiming current-series | ✅ line 21 already reads `(current series: 17.0.0, released 2026-08-14)` — #8882 has landed |

House style confirmed on the same read: v15 ⇒ `(final release: 15.1.1)`, v14 ⇒ `(final release: 14.8.0)`.

⚠️ **One thing the card's quote omits.** The live blockquote carries a trailing clause the card did not reproduce:

> (15.1.1 was a small patch on the previous line — better-auth family pinning and auth-plugin init isolation — covered by the [v15 page](/docs/releases/v15).)

That sentence is **still true** and is a cross-reference, not pre-mode framing. ⛔ It must survive the rewrite. The card's "the section-headings-say-16.0.0-for-brevity sentence can go" applies to *that* sentence only.

## Sequencing — why #8892 is held back rather than batched

**#8892 is the gate that would catch this class** ("nothing fails when a GA'd major's release page still describes itself as a pre-release"). If the gate lands while this page is still stale, **`main` goes red** — a shared-infrastructure break every lane pays for. So the instance lands first and the gate follows. #8892 stays in the queue until this merges. ⛔ Do not implement any part of #8892 here.

## Guardrail — this PR is the sanctioned exception, and it is narrow

`content/docs/releases/` is release-owned: release notes are written centrally at release time, and a **code** PR that edits them is the exact thing that guardrail exists to stop. The sanctioned remedy for a factual error is a **dedicated docs-only PR**, which is what this is. ⇒ ⛔ Not one byte outside the two named files; ⛔ no code, no changeset content, no rider of any kind. `skip-changeset`.

⚠️ ⛔ **Do not touch `v17.mdx`.** A `chore: version packages` PR (#8653) is open and a release may be in progress; v17's page was just compiled by #8882 and is not this card's business.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #8912. And a dispatch instruction of mine that was simply wrong.

### ⛔ First: my prompt overrode a standing contract, and it should not have

The dev raised this rather than silently absorbing it. Its standing contract (`.claude/agents/os-dev.md`) says it files out-of-scope findings itself, as unassigned cards. **My dispatch said "report it and I will file it."** It followed my prompt.

**My prompt was wrong.** Unconditional conditions live in the role file, and when a dispatch prompt conflicts with it, **the role file wins** — dispatch words exist to carry the *increment*, not to override standing terms. Raising the conflict instead of picking one silently is exactly right, and the reasoning attached to it is the part worth keeping:

> parallel devs cannot see each other's same-hour filings, so an unfiled finding is the one that gets re-derived.

⇒ Findings now filed by me, since my instruction created the gap: **#8916** and **#8917**. ⚠️ Future dispatches from this seat will not restate or override os-dev's filing contract.

### Verdict: ACCEPT

Verified against GitHub, ⛔ not against the report:

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | draft ✓ · base **`85f5e78`** (current `main`, branched fresh) ✓ · `Fixes #8886` ✓ |
| changed files | **2**, `+21/−14` — `v16.mdx` + `index.mdx`, exactly the declared surface ✓ |
| `v17.mdx` | untouched ✓ (`chore: version packages` #8653 still open) |
| index v16 entry | `(final release: 16.1.0)` — matches the v15/v14 closed-series house style ✓ |
| labels | `skip-changeset` applied **and read back after the bots settled** ✓ |
| gates | 7 families, judged by **exit status** ✓ |

**The dates check out against the right instrument.** All four (`rc.0` 07-19, `rc.1` 07-20, GA 07-21, `16.1.0` 07-22) match the **tag-object** creation dates. ⚠️ My own first pass used `git log --format=%cs <tag>` — the *commit* date — which disagrees on `rc.0` (07-20) and would have had me flag a correct date as wrong. Tag date is the authority for "when was it cut"; commit date is not.

**The 15.1.1 cross-reference survived verbatim**, as instructed. ⚠️ Also worth recording: my first check for it was a multi-word `grep` that returned **0**, because the sentence *wraps across two lines* and a line-oriented literal can never match it. A zero-hit with no positive control is not evidence — I re-read the blockquote before speaking, which is the only reason this is a footnote and not a false REWORK.

### What lifts this above the card

The card named **one** stale surface. The sweep I asked for in Zone 2 found **four**, and the two nobody had noticed are the interesting ones: *"Console vs. pin"* and *"Console changes after the `rc.0` pin"* both still framed a pin move as unreleased-on-`main`, when it had shipped as `@objectstack/console` 16.0.0-rc.1 (changeset `1965549`).

The `Landed since 16.0.0-rc.0` window **was** left open, and closing it was done by evidence rather than assertion: all ten entries mapped to changeset ids consumed at the `16.0.0-rc.1` cut, plus the `## 16.0.0` sections re-listing the rc.0 and rc.1 entries — the signature of `changeset pre exit` — to establish the window shipped in GA.

And a self-correction I want on the record because it is a genuine trap: a text search for `#3354` hits several **17.0.0** changelog entries that are **objectui's** issue numbering, not this repo's. Matching by content put it in `16.0.0-rc.1`. ⚠️ **Bare issue numbers are not unique across repos** — a cross-repo grep will confirm whatever you already believed.

### Two more corrections to my dispatch, both accepted

1. **`check:doc-links` does not exist in this repo.** I named it as "likely". `check:adr-links` is the only link gate and it covers `docs/adr/` only. The dev re-derived the real set and added `check:doc-anchors` on its own reasoning (the diff sits beside two `#landed-since-1600-rc0` fragment links). ⚠️ Naming a gate I had not verified is the same "PM hazard notice pointing at the wrong thing" failure I have logged twice today; the re-derive-from-the-tree instruction is what caught it.
2. **`check:doc-anchors` needed `github-slugger`, absent from every `node_modules` in the container** — correctly treated as a real blocker rather than a silent skip, and resolved with `pnpm install --ignore-scripts` under `flock`. ⛔ "Could not run" reported as "ran" is the failure that instruction exists to prevent.

### ⚠️ Sequencing — my plan for #8892 was wrong, and this PR does not fix it

I held #8892 behind this card on the reasoning that the gate must not land before the page it would go red on. The reasoning holds; **my instance set did not**. Re-verified independently: `v9.mdx` (says 9.0.0, tag `9.11.0`), `v12.mdx` (12.0.0, tag `12.6.0`) and `v14.mdx` (*current:* 14.5.0, tag `14.8.0`, and its index entry already disagrees with it) are stale too.

⇒ **Merging this PR does not make `main` safe for #8892.** Filed as **#8916** with the three scope options, and recorded on #8892 itself so it cannot be dispatched into that trap.

**Next**: confirming this PR's gate job conclusions, then ready → auto-merge → MERGED. ⚠️ Surfaced in the round report as a `content/docs/releases/**` (release-owned) PR so the maintainer has a veto window before it queues.
